castle_page.title: The Castle of Caccamo
castle_page.rhyme_1:
In a Norman castle forged by time,
come, admire, stop for a while.
It's not just stone, nor a cold rampart,
but an ancient soul awaiting your gaze.
castle_page.history_intro: The Castle was built in 1094 by order of Count Roger I. Over the centuries it passed through 14 noble families — including the Chiaramonte, Cabrera and De Spuches — until 1963, when it was handed over to the Sicilian Region.
castle_page.towers: The Torre Mastra, the oldest and tallest, holds a cistern at its base. The Torre Gibellina watches over Terravecchia, while the Torre della Fossa closes off the southern front.
castle_page.size_note: One of the best-preserved Norman castles in Sicily: walking through it all takes at least an hour, between courtyards and walkways.
castle_page.biglietti: Tickets — Full price €6 · Reduced online €4.50 · Residents €1 · Students 18-25 €3 · Free under 18.

chiese_page.poesia_intro:
Five temples of stone, of faith and memory,
open their doors onto centuries of history.
chiese_page.poesia_outro: Let yourself be guided where time has stood still...
chiese_page.verse_cappuccini:
At the top of the Capuchins the journey begins,
between an altarpiece and a wide, favourable horizon.
chiese_page.verse_angeli:
At the Angels' church rests, in the most sacred silence,
the Blessed Giovanni, emblem of the village.
chiese_page.verse_annunziata:
Then the Annunziata reveals its painted vaults,
and the bell tower never conquered by its guards.
chiese_page.verse_badia:
Further down, the Badia dresses the earth in flowers,
with a majolica embroidery of rare splendour.
chiese_page.verse_duomo:
Enter the great Duomo, majestic and solemn,
among Gagini's marbles and the ever-present Stomer altarpiece.

cibo_eventi_page.subtitle: Four seasons, four ways to experience Caccamo
cibo_eventi_page.cta: Ask the Castellana to tell you about it
cibo_eventi_page.s1_body: The Sausage Festival opens the autumn, alongside local sweets like taralli. In December the village lights up with nativity scenes: the one at the Capuchins, set up outside the convent with antique farm tools and household objects from 40-60 years ago, and the one at Santo Domenico, among the most beautiful to see. Below the Castle, the great Christmas tree is lit, and the neighbouring towns — easily reached by local transport — often host live nativity scenes.
cibo_eventi_page.s1_tags: Sausage Festival · Capuchins' Nativity Scene · Santo Domenico Nativity Scene · Tree below the Castle
cibo_eventi_page.s2_body: The week opens on Palm Sunday with U Signuruzzu a Cavaddu, when a local child plays Jesus in the entry into Jerusalem. Good Friday evening brings the living Way of the Cross: the Madonna with the pierced heart meets Christ on a bed of roses. The same day, it is customary to "visit the sepulchres" — churches left open, altars set up with sprouted wheat, recalling Mary and Magdalene going to Christ's tomb.
cibo_eventi_page.s2_tags: U Signuruzzu a Cavaddu — Palm Sunday · Living Way of the Cross — Good Friday · Visiting the sepulchres · Supper Bread · Almond "little sheep"
cibo_eventi_page.s3_body: Not just any saint, but a patron who is truly Caccamo's own: the Blessed Giovanni Liccio is a son of the village, which is why his feast is among the most heartfelt by the community. The procession crosses the whole town, especially the old quarter — a unique way to see the village in a different light and feel part of the community.
cibo_eventi_page.s3_tags: Patronal procession · Patron saint of Caccamo · Historic centre
cibo_eventi_page.s4_body: Three days of celebration: the Castellana's historic parade opens the festivities, leading up to the Palio that closes Caccamo's summer.
cibo_eventi_page.s4_tags: Historic parade · Palio · Feast of San Nicasio
cibo_eventi_page.s5_body: A whole summer of music, theatre, sports and traditions at the foot of the Castle: from the Opera Singing Master Class to Sicilian music evenings, from the Historic Parade of the Castellana to band concerts, up to the Pizza Festival and the National Karting Trophy. A rich calendar that accompanies the village from July to September.
cibo_eventi_page.s5_tags: Opera Singing Master Class · Historic Parade of the Castellana · Band Concerts · Pizza Festival · National Karting Trophy

canti_page.page_title: Songs and Prayers of the Village
canti_page.subtitle: Family voices, passed down in dialect
canti_page.legend_title: Sister Felicia and the Pomegranate Challenge
canti_page.legend_p1: The majestic Castle of Caccamo, perched on its imposing limestone cliff, holds one of the most fascinating and mysterious stories in all of Sicily: the legend of Sister Felicia, also known as the nun of the castle.
canti_page.legend_p2: It is said that Felicia, a girl of extraordinary beauty, was the daughter of the castellan of the time — most likely a nobleman of the Cabrera or Chiaramonte family. As in every proper chivalric drama, the young woman committed the greatest sin for the nobility of that era: she fell madly in love with a young man of humble origins, a page or a young soldier of the castle garrison.
canti_page.legend_p3: When her strict father discovered the secret relationship, his reaction was furious. He had the young lover arrested and locked away in the castle's dark dungeons — according to some versions, thrown into one of the notorious razor wells. To punish his daughter and stifle the scandal, he forced her to take vows, shutting her away for life in an enclosed convent.
canti_page.legend_p4: The girl took the name Sister Felicia. Consumed by grief for her lost love, she died of a broken heart at a young age. But her bond with the castle was too strong to be broken by death: it is said her tormented soul returned there, and still wanders it to this day.
canti_page.legend_p5: On nights of the full moon, as midnight strikes, the ghost of the nun appears among the silent halls, dressed in a white gown, beautiful and melancholic. In her hands she clutches a silver tray bearing a ripe pomegranate, red as blood.
canti_page.legend_p6: If a brave visitor meets her at midnight, she does not frighten him: she comes towards him and offers him the tray, proposing a challenge. He must shell the pomegranate and eat every single seed, without using his hands and without letting even one fall to the ground.
canti_page.legend_p7: If he succeeds, the spell is broken: Sister Felicia shows him the exact spot where an immense treasure is hidden in the castle's dungeons, before flying up to heaven, finally at peace. If he fails, even by dropping a single seed, the spectre vanishes instantly with a moan of disappointment, leaving the unfortunate visitor in the dark.
canti_page.legend_p8: The choice of the pomegranate is no coincidence: in Mediterranean mythology it has always been the fruit of the realm of the dead and of unbreakable bonds, as in the Greek myth of Persephone, condemned to remain in Hades for eating six pomegranate seeds. In the legend of Sister Felicia, the fruit represents the eternal bond with the afterlife and the broken passion of the two young lovers, sacrificed on the altar of noble pride.
canti_page.legend_p9: To this day, it is said that no one has ever managed to pass the test. Sister Felicia continues to wait, with her silver tray and her untouched pomegranate.
canti_page.legend_cta: Ask the Castellana to tell you the story

about.title: The Vision of Amunì
about.mission: Amunì was born from the desire to reconnect the present with its roots. It's not just a tourist website: it's a digital ecosystem that tells, accompanies and brings to life the heritage of Caccamo — voice after voice, monument after monument.
about.service_details: The Castellana is the beating heart of this project: an intelligent audioguide that speaks 5 languages and accompanies you in front of every monument, telling you verified stories that no plaque could ever contain. With the Premium service, her voice opens up even further: unique routes, local logistics, hidden gems nearby (Pietra Piatta, Vetrana, the Ombelico di Venere), building a natural bridge between Caccamo and the neighbouring villages.
about.insider_value: Every legend, every song in dialect, every stone of this village now has a carefully crafted voice telling its story, in natural, flowing language. The Castellana doesn't recite a rigid script, nor does she make anything up: she only holds the truths of the territory, passed down with the care of someone who truly knows them.

chi_siamo.title: About Us: A Story of Vision
chi_siamo.founder_bio: The Amunì project was born from my double nature: the analytical precision of a chemistry researcher and a passion, self-taught, for programming. I had no background in computer science: I learned by trying, one attempt after another, driven by the desire to tell the story, as it deserves, of a territory I felt had been overlooked for too many years.
chi_siamo.philosophy: From that desire came the Castellana: not just a chatbot, but a carefully crafted guide who accompanies the visitor — a living audioguide that gives voice back to the stones, legends and dialect songs of Caccamo, in five different languages. I don't see this project as a finished destination, but as a living laboratory: popular culture is a dynamic heritage, and I believe that valuing a territory also means preserving the voices of those who live there, passing on traditions, nursery rhymes and songs to future generations.
chi_siamo.freemium_model: The historical and monumental content is a public good, accessible to everyone. The 'Castellana Premium' experience is reserved for those who want a deeper journey: exclusive access to technical analysis of the heritage, layered stories and personalised support for an authentic, timeless discovery.
chi_siamo.events: Every image, every animation, every line of code in Amunì — and every word spoken by the Castellana — was thought out and built from my smartphone, between my research work and my two little girls. If you've made it this far, you're part of this small laboratory too.

home.poetry:
Beyond the horizon where the lake becomes a mirror and glory,
Caccamo weaves its breath into ancient memory.
It's not just stone defying ages and people,
hiding surprising treasures within its walls.

Like a ball of yarn slowly unwinding,
it spreads through every alley, in every small story.
A weave of centuries revealed with love and mystery,
for those seeking the beating heart of a true village.

Amunì, take the path,
the Castellana is here to keep you company.
home.castellana_intro_text: Talk to the Castellana: your multilingual tourist guide to discover stories, hidden gems and flavour trails among the wonders of the village and surrounding area.
home.premium_text: For €3.90, you get access to the Castellana for 4 days: the multilingual guide who knows every secret of Caccamo, from transport to the hidden gems of the area.
